new_results.statement: For 4/3<r<2, p=r/(r-1), alpha=r-1, if K(z)=||p_{T_z}||_p and E K(Z)^p<infinity in the partner receiver setup, then ||p_Q||inf <=2^{3alpha/(2r)}(2-r)^(-1/r)R0^(-alpha/r)[E K(Z)^p]^(1/p). Cellwise core localization therefore costs only (sum m_j K_j^p)^(1/p) if the score remains whole.

For a driver submeasure of mass m whose score pushforward has density cap L, the output submeasure obeys ||p_eta||inf <=K_r 2^{2alpha/r}(2-r)^(-1/r)m^(1/r)L^(alpha/r). Mass-homogeneous score caps L_j<=Hm_j make arbitrary countable mixtures zero-loss.

Leaving W whole with d!=0 gives L_j<=m_j/(2|d|) under arbitrary positive fragmentation of the full driver law, hence zero localization tax. Keeping one Z_k whole gives the analogous result with |c_k|. Applied to partner Q_m, arbitrary Z-bank fragmentation keeps the exact 13.0770828465 bound.

For Q_N=U1^2+U2^2+2Z_NW with Z_N uniform on N remote intervals of width 1/N, the whole score gives a uniform 5.4051317350 certificate while cellwise mass-cap payment gives 5.4051317350 N^(5/12) and normalize-rescale-first partner payment gives 6.2448335270 N^(5/12). Claude Theorem B controls the true density by 8sqrt(2pi). This is a proof-order obstruction only.
